title: IMPLEMENTATION OF SASCI SCHEME
body_text:
With the aim to develop iconic tourist centres in the country, the Ministry of Tourism issued operational guidelines along with detailed project report template under Special Assistance to the States for Capital Investment (SASCI)-Development of Iconic Tourist Centres to Global Scale initiative scheme.
As per the guidelines, the proposals were invited from the State Governments for considering financial assistance to the States under the scheme. The parameters formulated for examining the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) submitted by the States covered connectivity to the site, existing tourism eco-system at site/destination, carrying capacity, availability of utility services, project impact and value envisaged which included expected increase in tourist footfall, increase tourist spend, new employment opportunities, attracting private investment etc. Accordingly, 40 projects were sanctioned across 23 States in the country including two projects in the state of Karnataka by the Government of India under the scheme for ₹3295.76 Crore in the financial year 2024-25 with 100% central funding and the details of these projects is annexed.
Further, Department of Expenditure amended SASCI guidelines for 2025-26 and as per amended guidelines, States which did not avail funds under Part-III of SASCI 2024-25 are eligible to avail Special Assistance of not more than Rs.250 crores for tourism projects under Part-II of SASCI 2025-26. As per amended guidelines, Special Assistance of Rs.250 crores have been sanctioned and released each to Nagaland, Mizoram and Himachal Pradesh for tourism projects under Part-II of SASCI 2025-26 and the details of sanction is also annexed.
The projects sanctioned under the SASCI are regularly monitored at various levels. The Guidelines for SASCI, includes National Institutional Framework comprising of Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), Mission Directorate (MD) etc. and State Institutional Framework. The Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC) and Mission Directorate (MD) includes representatives of the Ministries/Departments concerned with Culture, Housing and Urban Affairs, Civil Aviation, Road Transport and Highways, Ports, Environment and Forests, Rural Development, Railways and the Archaeological Survey of India, among others, to facilitate convergence & coordinated development. Project DPRs are also required to incorporate the applicable statutory clearances, carrying-capacity considerations, stakeholder consultations and sustainable operation and maintenance arrangements.
The Ministry has also developed a Program Management Information System (PMIS) for monitoring of its destination development related schemes as a unified digital platform to facilitate seamless information, communication, sharing and reporting system in respect of the projects undertaken as part of its various schemes. Ministry of Tourism and SGs/UTAs including project implementing agencies are integral part of this system.
This information was given by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat in a reply in Rajya Sabha today.

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Tourism informed Rajya Sabha about implementation of the SASCI (Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment) scheme for developing iconic tourist centres. In FY 2024-25, 40 tourism projects across 23 states were sanctioned for ₹3295.76 crore with 100% central funding, evaluated on parameters like connectivity, carrying capacity, and expected tourism/employment impact. In FY 2025-26, under amended guidelines, ₹250 crore each was sanctioned and released to Nagaland, Mizoram, and Himachal Pradesh, states that hadn't availed Part-III funds earlier.
enrichment.context:
SASCI is a Department of Expenditure scheme providing 50-year interest-free loans to states for capital investment, with Ministry of Tourism administering a dedicated component for developing tourism infrastructure to global standards. This reflects the government's push to leverage tourism as an economic driver, given its potential for employment generation, foreign exchange earnings, and regional development, especially in states with lesser fiscal space for capital expenditure. The scheme's 100% central funding model is notable since it bypasses typical centrally sponsored scheme cost-sharing patterns, effectively incentivizing states to undertake capital projects without straining state budgets.

The institutional architecture—Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), Mission Directorate, and a Program Management Information System (PMIS)—indicates an attempt at cooperative federalism and inter-ministerial convergence, involving Culture, Housing and Urban Affairs, Civil Aviation, Railways, Ports, Environment, and ASI. This mirrors similar convergence-based approaches seen in other flagship schemes like PRASHAD and Swadesh Darshan, aiming to avoid fragmented, siloed infrastructure development. The scheme's DPR evaluation criteria—covering carrying capacity, statutory clearances, and stakeholder consultation—also reflect growing emphasis on sustainable tourism development amid concerns about over-tourism at heritage and ecological sites in India.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI)' scheme, under which iconic tourist centres are being developed, is administered by which ministry/department for its overall framework?
options: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the Department of Expenditure amended the SASCI guidelines, indicating it is the nodal department for the overall scheme, while Ministry of Tourism administers the tourism-specific component.

prelims_questions.question: Under the SASCI-Development of Iconic Tourist Centres scheme, what is the funding pattern for sanctioned projects?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states the 40 projects sanctioned in FY 2024-25 were funded with 100% central funding.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of the SASCI scheme in promoting tourism infrastructure development in India. Examine the institutional mechanisms established for ensuring inter-ministerial convergence and sustainable project implementation.

Tourism has significant potential for employment generation and regional economic development in India. Analyze the challenges in balancing tourism infrastructure development with environmental sustainability and carrying capacity concerns, citing recent government initiatives.
